summary: Hitoshi Inui is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held posts at Koyasan University as a lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and later as a professor (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Kato works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Attested as a lecturer and research assistant in 1992, he later served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017) and held a post at Otani University.

Hitoshi Miyake is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1956) and Keio University (~1956–1963). He served as a professor at Keio University (~1975–1999) and Kokugakuin University (~1999–2004).

Hitoshi Obara is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Hokkaido University (~1963–1967), he served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1993–2015).

Linguist Hla Pe studied at the University of Rangoon (MA ~1931–1938), University College London (~1938–1939), and SOAS University of London (doctorate ~1940–1944). At SOAS, he taught Burmese starting in 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington by 1994, studying under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Hogen Bays is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada. He has served as co-abbot at Great Vow Zen Monastery.

Hojun Nagasaki specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1961–1964). He served as professor emeritus at Otani University (~1978–1999) and as president of the Japanese Association for Jain Studies in 1998.
Hokai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.

Hokei Idzumi (1884–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University (~1903–1907) and under Bunyiu Nanjio (~1904–1908), later serving as a professor at Otani University (~1923–1947).

Holly Gayley works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies in Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Harvard University (~2002–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado (~2008).

Holmes Welch (1924–1981) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1946–1957) under Francis Woodman Cleaves, later serving as a lecturer at Harvard (~1963–1981) and Yale University.

Hong Luo specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning a PhD from Peking University by 2007. He worked at the China Tibetology Research Center (2007–2017) and became a religious studies professor at Sichuan University in 2018.
Hongyue Guo works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo earned a PhD from Indiana University (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and also studied under Xubang Qi.

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996), and director of the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh is a scholar in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University by 2004, where he studied under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales (1900–1981) studied at Queens' College, Cambridge, and SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden (PhD 1931). He served as Field Director for the Greater-India Research Committee (~1934–1941) and Vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1947–1968).

Horace Hayman Wilson (1786–1860) studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. An Indologist, he served as Assay Master at the Kolkata Mint (1816–1833), Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1831–1860), and director of the Royal Asiatic Society (1837).

Horace L. Friess (1900–1975) was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Columbia University (~1915–1918) and Heidelberg (~1922–1923). He held posts at Johns Hopkins and Columbia, where he was appointed Buttenwieser Professor (1962–1966).
Horkhang Sonam Palbar (1919–1995) was a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Tsadru Ngawang Losang and Gendun Chophel (~1946–1951).
